docs.title: blackhole-sec
docs.text:
Four small tools I reach for every day, in one install. Everything runs offline. Nothing phones home.

- :material-link-off: **check** Paste a sketchy link, get a score and a reason. Never fetches the URL. - :material-lock: **vault** Passwords and files in one encrypted store on your disk. Argon2id + AES-256-GCM. - :material-image-off: **shred** See photo metadata, strip it, or delete for real. - :material-package-variant-closed: **bundle** Encrypted `.bhb` archives instead of zip. Names and contents hidden; optional keyfile second factor. 
pip install blackhole-sec
# or without touching pip yourself:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Satin-networks/blackhole-sec/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

blackhole check "http://secure-paypal-login.tk/free-nitro"
blackhole vault init
blackhole shred analyze photo.jpg
blackhole bundle create ./mydir ./backup.bhb

Start with Checking links if you live in Discord DMs, or Everyday recipes for copy-paste flows.

Companion to wisp, our local WireGuard manager. Wisp moves the packets, blackhole keeps the rest of your life tidy.

docs.title: Bundles (.bhb)
docs.text:
Three flavors. With a password, .bhb packs a directory to tar.gz and encrypts the whole thing, names and all - only blackhole opens it. Add --keyfile and the password becomes half the key: the file is a second factor, and a stolen copy of the bundle cannot even be attacked offline without it. With --no-password it packs plain: no encryption, opens with no flags, same as a zip with no password. Pick per bundle.

Password mode is deliberately expensive to open - that is the point. Every guess an attacker makes costs the full Argon2id work below, per try. Unlocking in a terminal takes a few seconds; that is the trade.

--kdf preset memory passes work vs the old default light 64 MiB 3 1x (what 0.2.x used) hard (default) 1 GiB 8 ~42x paranoid 2 GiB 12 ~128x

docs.title: Creating one
docs.text:
# password mode (prompts twice)
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb

# let blackhole make a strong password and print it once
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --generate

# two factors: opens only with the password and this file, both
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --keyfile ~/bh-photos.key

# the heaviest settings (wants a few GiB of RAM free)
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --kdf paranoid

# plain mode: no password, no extra files, anyone can open it
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --no-password

Weak passwords are rejected before anything is written: shorter than 12 characters, fewer than three character classes under 16, the usual top-list classics, repeated runs and keyboard walks. --generate sidesteps all of that with a 24-character random password. Store it before you close the terminal.

With --keyfile PATH the bundle key becomes Argon2id(password) mixed with SHA-256 of that file. Opening needs both, and someone holding only the bundle cannot test password guesses at all - there is nothing to check them against. If PATH does not exist, a random 32-byte keyfile is minted there (0600). Keep it somewhere else than the bundle: a USB stick, or a copy in the vault, not the same folder.

docs.title: Opening one
docs.text:
blackhole bundle extract ./photos.bhb ./restored

Password-mode bundles prompt for the password themselves; plain bundles need nothing. Two-factor bundles take --keyfile PATH too, or prompt for the path when you have a terminal. A wrong password, wrong keyfile, or tampered file all get the same clean refusal - the bundle cannot tell you which part is off, and that is on purpose. A wrong password re-prompts, up to three tries, then gives up cleanly. There is no partial extract. Bundles made back when --no-password wrote a .key file still open with --keyfile, nothing else changed for them.

docs.title: Peeking without unpacking
docs.text:
blackhole bundle list ./photos.bhb
blackhole bundle verify ./photos.bhb; echo $?

list prints every file with its size. verify only checks the password/key and authenticity: exit 0 opens, 1 does not.

docs.title: Root-owned files
docs.text: create never deletes or moves your source; it only reads it. If a bundle (or its directory) belongs to root, run the same command with sudo - blackhole says so in the error. Files created that way are root-owned too, including anything you extract.

docs.title: How it compares to zip
docs.text:
Problem with zip What .bhb password mode does ZipCrypto breaks in minutes Argon2id (heavy, per-bundle params) into AES-256-GCM Weak passwords get guessed in minutes Creation rejects them; --generate makes real ones The password is the whole story --keyfile adds a second factor; a leaked bundle can't be tested offline Filenames visible without the password Names are inside the encrypted blob ZipSlip (../../evil) on extract Absolute paths, .., symlinks and devices are skipped Every website unzips it Only blackhole reads .bhb

The full head-to-head with age and 7-Zip is on the comparison page.

docs.title: Format v1
docs.text:
Big-endian, one header, one payload:

BHB1 | kdf_id | t,m,p | salt | [nonce (12)] | ct_len (u64) | ct

kdf_id 1 (password), 3 (password + keyfile), and 0 (old keyfile) carry a nonce and ct is AES-GCM with the header as AAD. kdf_id 2 (plain) has no nonce and ct is the tar.gz as-is.

The t,m,p numbers are per bundle: the reader derives with whatever the header says, so files written by older versions keep opening with their original, lighter numbers. Absurd values are rejected before a single byte is hashed, so a crafted file cannot ask your machine for more RAM than it has.

Implementation lives in src/blackhole_sec/bundle/__init__.py. It is short enough to read in one sitting, which is intentional.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Bundle the cleaned copies (*.cleaned.jpg), not the originals, when you share photos with other people.
  • .bhb files are chmod 0600 on creation. Copy them normally, perms do not survive every filesystem, so check after moving.
  • Write the password down somewhere real, or keep it in the vault. There is no recovery, and with these numbers there will never be one.

• bundle create --keyfile PATH adds a second factor: the bundle key becomes Argon2id(password) mixed with the keyfile's hash, so opening needs both and a leaked bundle cannot even be tested offline. A missing keyfile path is minted on the spot (32 random bytes, 0600).
  • The docs have a head-to-head with age and 7-Zip now.
  • The vault stores files now: vault add-file PATH (64 MiB cap) keeps a copy inside, vault export LABEL [--out DEST] writes it back with a checksum check. The bytes sit encrypted in a <vault>.files directory beside the vault, so ordinary password lookups stay quick.
  • Vault prompts are friendlier: type a master of your own, press Enter at any password prompt to get one generated, and a weak master warns instead of refusing. vault init --kdf light|hard|paranoid picks the work factor for the machine it will live on.
  • vault list shows each entry's kind and a real date. vault get on a stored file points you at vault export.
  • blackhole upgrade no longer dies on externally managed pythons (PEP 668); it falls back to a user-site install with pip.
  • The readme and docs carry a logo now.

• .bhb bundles are much harder to crack. Password mode now runs Argon2id at 1 GiB and 8 passes by default - ~42x the work of 0.2.x per guess - and bundle create --kdf paranoid roughly triples that again (~128x). Unlock takes a few seconds now; that is the point.
  • Old bundles keep opening unchanged: the work factor lives in the header as t/m/p, and the reader derives with whatever it finds. Absurd header values are rejected before any memory is spent.
  • Weak bundle passwords are refused at creation (12+ chars, three classes under 16, no top-list classics, no keyboard walks) and bundle create --generate prints a fresh 24-char password for you.
  • bundle extract/list/verify detect encrypted bundles and prompt for the password themselves; a wrong password re-prompts up to three tries. --password still works, it just stopped being required.
  • Passphrase generation now draws from the EFF large wordlist (7776 words, ~64 bits for five) instead of a 26-word rump.
  • Derived bundle keys are zeroed after use (best effort in Python).

• --no-password now packs plain and unencrypted: no keyfile, opens with no flags. Password mode is unchanged and still fully encrypted.
  • Old keyfile bundles from 0.2.x still open.
  • Damaged bundles report cleanly instead of tracebacking.

• Permission errors on root-owned files now say so and suggest sudo.
  • bundle create prints that the source was left untouched.
  • Installer scripts go system-wide under sudo (/usr/local).

• Color throughout: severity-colored signals, score bars, graded audit scores. --json/--csv stay plain. --no-color (or NO_COLOR, or a pipe) turns it off.
  • New: vault rm, vault passwd, bundle list, bundle verify, intake --json.
  • Fixed: bundles keep empty directories; huge directories spill to disk instead of RAM; corrupt bundles say so instead of tracebacking; malformed URLs can't crash check; clipboard copies use persistent tools first and no longer promise an auto-clear that never happened.
  • Leaner install: dropped two unused dependencies.

• Every command documents its arguments with examples (COMMAND -h, plus -h short flag everywhere).
  • New blackhole upgrade (and --check) for self-updates from PyPI.
  • Curl installer trio: scripts/install.sh, update.sh, uninstall.sh.
  • CLI version now reads installed package metadata, no more drift.
  • Filesystem failures (permission denied, missing vault, bad password) print one-line errors instead of tracebacks.

docs.title: 0.1.0 - first public cut
docs.text:
• check: offline link scoring, 25+ signals, JSON/CSV/batch, exit codes.
  • vault: Argon2id plus AES-256-GCM store, generator, audit.
  • shred: analyze, clean, verify, shred with 1/3/7 passes.
  • bundle: .bhb encrypted archives, password and keyfile modes.
  • intake: link plus file triage in one command.
  • Docs site (this), CI, pip packaging as blackhole-sec.

docs.title: Checking links
docs.text: blackhole check reads the URL as text and scores it. It never opens the page, never does DNS, never calls an API. Safe to run on the nastiest "free nitro" lure.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
blackhole check "http://secure.paypal.com.evil.tk/login"

MALICIOUS 68/100 (HIGH) hxxp[:]//secure[.]paypal[.]com[.]evil[.]tk/login
  +18 brand_impersonation: brand=paypal host=secure.paypal.com.evil.tk
  +10 suspicious_tld: .tk
  + 8 suspicious_keywords: login,secure

Notice the output is defanged (hxxp[://], [.]) so it can't be clicked by accident.

docs.title: Scores
docs.text:
Range Verdict What I do 0-20 BENIGN Carry on 21-49 SUSPICIOUS Hover, verify sender, don't log in 50-100 MALICIOUS Don't touch it

Confidence (VERY_LOW to HIGH) is based on how many signals fired. Every signal prints its weight, the evidence, and a MITRE tag like T1566.002 so you can look it up.

docs.title: Batch and scripts
docs.text:
# a list of links
blackhole check -f urls.txt --json > report.json

# from a pipe
echo "http://paypal-secure.tk/login" | blackhole check --file -

# CSV for a spreadsheet
blackhole check -f urls.txt --csv > report.csv

# fail the build on anything scary
blackhole check "http://evil.tk/x" --threshold 50; echo $?
# exit 2 means something scored at or above the threshold

docs.title: What it looks at
docs.text:
Short version: IP hosts, punycode and homoglyphs, shorteners, odd TLDs, long URLs, deep paths, tons of subdomains or hyphens, @ tricks, missing https, weird ports, heavy percent-encoding, high entropy, lure words (login, nitro, wallet), .exe-style paths, open-redirect params, brand names in the wrong domain, near-miss typos (paypa1), free-hosting domains, digit-heavy names, and embedded credentials.

Long version lives in src/blackhole_sec/check/features.py - it's one readable file, tweak the lists to taste.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Lexical only. It can't catch a hacked WordPress page on a legit domain, and brand-new lure words need adding by hand. That's the trade for never touching the network.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: Every command documents itself. Whatever is here, blackhole COMMAND -h says it better, since it is generated from the same code.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• -h works everywhere as a short --help.
  • --no-color on any command (or the NO_COLOR env var) disables colors. --json and --csv are always plain.
  • Secrets are typed into hidden prompts, never passed as flags (so they stay out of shell history).
  • Commands that inspect only (check, shred analyze, shred verify, vault list, vault audit) never change anything.
  • Filesystem failures print one line naming the file, never a traceback.

docs.title: blackhole check [URL]...
docs.text:
Score links without fetching them. Defanged output, JSON/CSV modes, exit code 2 when anything hits --threshold (default 50).

blackhole check "http://secure-paypal-login.tk/free-nitro"
blackhole check -f urls.txt --json > report.json
blackhole check suspect.tk/x --explain

docs.title: blackhole vault ...
docs.text:
init creates the vault, set/get store and fetch by SERVICE name, list shows names, audit scores password health, gen prints a fresh secret without storing it. add-file keeps a copy of any file (64 MiB cap) and export writes it back out, checksum verified.

blackhole vault init --vault ~/.blackhole/vault.db
blackhole vault set github --username alice --generate 24
blackhole vault get github --show
blackhole vault add-file ~/tax-2025.pdf
blackhole vault export tax-2025.pdf --out ~/back
blackhole vault rm old-forum --yes
blackhole vault passwd

--vault PATH on any subcommand points at a different vault file.

docs.title: blackhole shred ...
docs.text:
analyze scores metadata, clean writes *.cleaned copies, verify exits 0/1 for scripts, shred deletes for real.

blackhole shred analyze photo.jpg
blackhole shred clean *.jpg --out-dir ./clean --yes
blackhole shred verify photo.cleaned.jpg; echo $?
blackhole shred shred secret.txt --passes 7 --yes

docs.title: blackhole bundle ...
docs.text:
create packs SRC_DIR into OUT_FILE (.bhb), extract unpacks it, list shows contents without extracting, verify checks the password/key with exit 0/1. Encrypted bundles prompt for the password on their own; --kdf light|hard|paranoid sets how expensive a guess is (1 GiB x 8 by default); --generate makes a strong password for you; --keyfile PATH adds a second factor (the bundle then needs the password and that file both); --no-password packs plain with no encryption.

blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --generate
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --keyfile ~/bh-photos.key
blackhole bundle extract ./photos.bhb ./restored
blackhole bundle list ./photos.bhb
blackhole bundle verify ./photos.bhb; echo $?

docs.title: blackhole intake URL FILE [--json]
docs.text: One-shot triage for a DM with a link and an attachment: prints the link verdict plus the file metadata verdict. --json merges both into one machine-readable object.

docs.title: blackhole upgrade [--check]
docs.text:
Fetches the latest release from PyPI and installs it with pip. The one command here that needs network. --check only compares versions.

blackhole upgrade --check
blackhole upgrade

docs.title: Compared to age and 7-Zip
docs.text:
Both are good, both are older, and each beats this one somewhere. The honest table first.

blackhole-sec (.bhb) age 7-Zip (.7z) Cost of one password guess Argon2id, 1 GiB x 8 by default, carried per bundle scrypt, ~256 MiB by default (-W raises it) iterated SHA-256, memory-light, count fixed by the app Encryption AES-256-GCM, header authenticated ChaCha20-Poly1305 AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA256 Second factor optional keyfile: password + file both no no Directories built in (a tar.gz inside the blob) no, pipe a tar through it yes Filenames inside the ciphertext, always only if you tar before encrypting visible unless -mhe=on Weak passwords refused at creation accepted accepted Opens elsewhere blackhole only any age implementation just about anywhere Compression gzip none LZMA2, much better

docs.title: Where they win
docs.text:
age has a written spec and independent implementations that agree on the bytes, plus security review work this project has not had. If interop matters, or you want a design with a name behind it, use age.

7-Zip is everywhere, has a GUI, and compresses far better. Its AES layer is fine; the difference is that testing guesses against a .7z is cheap in memory, so GPUs and dedicated rigs chew through them faster than they chew through a memory-hard KDF at similar wall-clock settings. That is the whole reason for Argon2id here.

docs.title: Where .bhb lands ahead
docs.text:
• Guessing is memory-hard and heavy by default, and the cost lives in each bundle's header, so new bundles can get steeper without breaking old ones.
  • The password can be only half the key. With --keyfile, a copy of the bundle alone cannot be tested offline at all.
  • Sloppy passwords are refused when the bundle is made, not after a loss.
  • Tags, sizes, and structure are inside the ciphertext, no flags needed.
  • Extraction refuses absolute paths, .., symlinks, and devices by default.

docs.title: The fine print
docs.text: Opening a hard bundle costs a few seconds and up to a gigabyte of RAM; paranoid about two. That is the point, but it is also a real cost on old machines, so --kdf light exists. .bhb has not been independently reviewed. The format is a page of code (src/blackhole_sec/bundle/__init__.py); read it before you bet anything you cannot lose on it. If you need third-party assurance today, age is the safer pick.

docs.title: Everyday recipes
docs.text: Copy-paste flows for the stuff I actually do week to week.

docs.title: Someone DMs you a "free nitro" link
docs.text:
blackhole check "http://discord-nitro-free.tk/claim?user=you"
# SUSPICIOUS or MALICIOUS -> don't log in, block and report

If they also sent a file, triage both at once:

blackhole intake "http://discord-nitro-free.tk/claim" ./qr-code.png

docs.title: Posting photos in a public server
docs.text:
blackhole shred analyze trip.jpg
blackhole shred clean trip.jpg
blackhole shred verify trip.cleaned.jpg && echo OK
# post trip.cleaned.jpg, keep or shred the original

docs.title: Storing a new account
docs.text:
blackhole vault set github --username alice --generate 24
blackhole vault audit   # run monthly, fix reused and short ones first

docs.title: Keeping a document in the vault
docs.text:
blackhole vault add-file ~/passport-scan.pdf
blackhole vault add-file ~/keys/api.pem --name stripe-key
blackhole vault list                                  # shows it as kind 'file'
blackhole vault export passport-scan.pdf --out ~/back # checksum verified
# the copy inside goes away with: blackhole vault rm passport-scan.pdf

docs.title: A backup bundle that needs two things
docs.text:
blackhole bundle create ./photos ./photos.bhb --generate --keyfile ~/bh-photos.key
# the generated password prints once: put it in the vault
# copy ~/bh-photos.key to a USB stick - not the same disk as the bundle
blackhole bundle extract ./photos.bhb ./restored --keyfile ~/bh-photos.key

docs.title: Sending a folder to a friend
docs.text:
blackhole bundle create ./project ./project.bhb
# send project.bhb over any channel, share the password over a
# different one (call them, don't put both in the same chat)

docs.title: Cleaning a whole folder before upload
docs.text:
for f in *.jpg; do blackhole shred clean "$f" --yes; done
blackhole shred verify *.cleaned.jpg
blackhole bundle create . ./upload.bhb --no-password
# upload upload.bhb - plain mode, so only for stuff that's fine public

docs.title: Checking a list from a mod queue
docs.text:
blackhole check -f reported-links.txt --csv > verdicts.csv
# sort by score, review the top of the list first

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text: How I think about this, plainly: what it covers and what it doesn't.

docs.title: Covered
docs.text:
• check never fetches URLs. Input capped at 2048 chars, output defanged. Safe to paste that "free nitro" link.
  • Stolen vault file: Argon2id (512 MiB, 8 passes by default, p=4) plus AES-256-GCM. The master is never stored. Files are 0600. Unlock is pass/fail against a verifier. vault passwd re-keys older vaults onto the current default, stored files included.
  • Posting photos: clean writes a new file, the original stays put. verify exits non-zero while sensitive tags remain.
  • .bhb archives encrypt names and contents as one blob. Password guesses run through Argon2id at 1 GiB and 8 passes by default (--kdf paranoid roughly triples that; the header carries the params, old bundles keep their own). With --keyfile, a stolen bundle cannot be tested offline at all without that file. Extraction skips absolute paths, .., symlinks and device nodes.

docs.title: Not covered
docs.text:
• An unlocked machine. Plaintext lives in memory while the vault is open. I lock after every command and clear the clipboard best-effort, but no local vault survives someone reading live RAM.
  • Weak passwords. Argon2id slows guessing, it doesn't rescue 123456. Bundle creation refuses the worst of them, and --generate/vault gen hand you a real one.
  • Malware. clean strips metadata, it doesn't sandbox anything.
  • Print-shop redaction. Image EXIF is fully stripped; PDFs are copied with a report of what's left. For legal-grade work use a dedicated tool.
  • Audits. Standard pieces, small readable code, but no third-party audit yet.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: Write privately with version, OS and steps. Keep vault files and bundles to yourself. See SECURITY.md in the repo root for the short version.

docs.title: Shredding files
docs.text: Photos quietly carry GPS, camera model, and timestamps. Handy for your own archive, bad for a public Discord post. Shred lets you look, strip, and, when you mean it, delete.

docs.title: The flow I use
docs.text:
blackhole shred analyze photo.jpg
# 40/100 photo.jpg tags=['GPSInfo', 'Model', 'DateTimeOriginal']

blackhole shred clean photo.jpg
# cleaned -> photo.cleaned.jpg, verify=PASS

blackhole shred verify photo.cleaned.jpg; echo $?
# PASS ... sensitive=[]

blackhole shred shred secret.txt --passes 3 --yes

Rules I stuck to:

  • clean never edits in place. It writes *.cleaned.* next to the original so you can't nuke the only copy by typo.
  • verify is script-friendly: exit 0 clean, 1 dirty.
  • shred overwrites (1, 3 or 7 passes), renames a few times to hide the name, then unlinks. SSDs can't promise much here - encryption plus shred is the honest combo - but spinning disks are properly gone.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text: JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF EXIF is fully stripped via Pillow. DOCX core props and PDF author fields are reported; PDFs are copied with a note of what's left rather than a false promise. Use a dedicated redaction tool for legal-grade PDFs.

docs.title: Watch out
docs.text: clean strips metadata, not malware. Don't open files you don't trust just because they're clean.

docs.title: Vault
docs.text: One encrypted file. One master password. No sync, no cloud, no recovery - which is exactly why there's nothing to breach.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
blackhole vault init --vault ~/.blackhole/vault.db

The file is created chmod 0600. Pick a long master and write it down somewhere safe. If you lose it, the vault is gone.

docs.title: Daily use
docs.text:
# save something (prompts for the rest)
blackhole vault set github --username alice --generate 24

# passphrases are nicer to type
blackhole vault set wifi --passphrase 5

# read it back
blackhole vault get github --show

# delete one you don't need (asks first unless --yes)
blackhole vault rm old-forum

# change the master (re-encrypts everything)
blackhole vault passwd

# copy without printing (best-effort clipboard, clears after ~30s)
blackhole vault get github

# what's in there
blackhole vault list

# fresh password without storing anything
blackhole vault gen --length 24

docs.title: Storing files
docs.text:
# keep a copy of a file in the vault (64 MiB cap)
blackhole vault add-file ~/tax-2025.pdf

# give it a shorter name if you like
blackhole vault add-file ~/keys/api.pem --name stripe-key

# write it back out (checksum checked, chmod 0600)
blackhole vault export stripe-key --out ~/keys/

# overwrite a copy you already exported
blackhole vault export tax-2025.pdf --force

vault list shows stored files with their size and original name, vault rm deletes the copy inside the vault (the file you added stays untouched), and vault passwd re-wraps everything under the new master.

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
blackhole vault audit

Score: 85/100  entries=12
reused passwords: {'hunter2...': ['old-forum', 'test-box']}
weak (<12 chars): ['router']
stale (>1y): ['bank-backup-code']

Change the reused and short ones first. That's the whole game.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Master + random 16-byte salt go through Argon2id (512 MiB, 8 passes by default; older vaults keep their own numbers until vault passwd) into a 32-byte key.
  • Everything is one JSON blob encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The header (magic, params, salt, nonce) is authenticated as AAD.
  • Unlock tries to decrypt a known verifier. Wrong password just fails.
  • The master is never written anywhere. Each command locks when it ends.
  • Stored files live in a <vault>.files directory beside the vault, each encrypted under its own HKDF subkey of the vault key. The vault file itself stays small, so ordinary lookups stay quick.
  • Generated passphrases draw from the EFF large wordlist (7776 words: five words is ~64 bits). Generated passwords default to 20 chars mixing letters, digits and symbols (~120 bits).

docs.title: Moving machines
docs.text: Copy the .db file - and the matching .files directory if you stored any files in it. That's it. Back both up like you'd back up anything precious - the backup is still encrypted, safe to keep on a USB stick.
